formal_context.note: Formal-only analyzer output was generated from the filtered trace section; bootstrap scheduler events and the 72915263ns filter transition were not fed into the formal analysis.

rate_context.replay_limitation: Replays captured boundary timestamps through real JointRate, not underlying workload or OS scheduling. Release delay includes caller work, pacing and scheduling; it does not identify their cause.

run.scope: owned ground scheduler diagnostic; not flight/long-run rate/Full

blocking_write.evidence: The formal trace has no sys_write entry/exit covering the worst group because that group starts after capture_stop_ns.
blocking_write.parser_note: Existing analyzer parse() treats unprefixed sys_write fd/count fields as hexadecimal, matching the trace print format.

model_wait.evidence: wire.jsonl has a step marker for tick 12180, but no diagnostic_step_cpu_timing row for tick 12180; retained diagnostic samples are periodic/slow samples.

diagnostic_native_input_timing.limitation: Retained slow(>2ms native wait)/periodic(tick%250) samples, not a full census. Each wait brackets only the supervisor wait_ap/wait_px4 call; acknowledge_ap, barrier/repair_input and all record writes are excluded and stay in the combined native_inputs stage. Supervisor off-CPU during a wait includes I/O wait and descheduling; it does not identify the native FC, host or Windows cause.

diagnostic_runtime_loop_timing.limitation: Sampled runtime intervals; pacing includes intended waits. Thread CPU and wall clocks have distinct read windows; no causal classification.

diagnostic_step_cpu_timing.limitation: Thread CPU separates execution from off-CPU time; off-CPU includes I/O wait and descheduling

model_wait.nearest_sample_note: Nearest samples end about 182ms before the worst group and cannot be used to attribute its lateness.

stage_assessment.overall: The exact worst group is temporally located, but this retained evidence cannot distinguish runqueue wait, blocking write, or model wait at that timestamp. The associations above are temporal evidence only and do not establish causality.

runqueue_wait.evidence: The formal trace has no scheduler events after event_ns_max; the worst group starts 203738653ns after capture_stop_ns.

formal_context_only.note: These are retained sampled waits, not a census and not the worst group.

by_native_path.native_path: AP then PX4 inputs; not separated

recorded_native_waits.limitation: Biased retained samples: whole-step wall time >2ms or tick divisible by 250. Counts/medians are not population rates; unpaired boundary intervals remain unaccounted. AP-only waits do not identify an AP function, thread, or host cause.

bootstrap.semantics: sched_switch-only retained window before precise filters

filter_transition.interpretation: The bootstrap and formal traces are not concatenated into one continuous scheduler interval.

boundaries.manager_boundary_note: report.finished_monotonic_ns is used as the available manager completion boundary; no rate group ends after the final logged group.

comparison.formal_and_post_order_of_magnitude_note: Formal groups already reach about 75.8ms lateness before capture stop. The 52 post-stop groups remain in the same 75.1-77.1ms end-lateness band; the maximum start-phase value is 77.256332ms. The timing logs show accumulation across the formal interval and no isolated teardown-sized jump, while they do not establish why the lateness accumulated.
comparison.window_limitation: The formal scheduler trace stops at formal_capture_stop_ns. Rate groups and sparse CPU timing continue later, but they cannot reconstruct scheduler or write causes during the uncovered interval or manager teardown.

cpu_timing.coverage_note: The sampled CPU timing rows do not exactly match any of the formal top-five group end ticks; no nearest sample is substituted.

cpu_timing.matching_rule: exact end_tick only; no nearest-sample attribution
